channel.title: HabitForge Docs
channel.description: A habit tracker that draws your consistency as a rope you watch thicken, with other people building theirs beside you.

item.title: White-label and licensing
item.description: Run HabitForge under your own name. We host it on your domain with your name and colours, on the web and Android; the source can also be bought outright.

item.title: What a white-label licence delivers
item.description: What the web and mobile platforms of a HabitForge licence include, what stays with us, and what a source buyout hands over.

item.title: White-label questions
item.description: What buyers ask first about licensing HabitForge, from source code and exclusivity to domains, store accounts and members' data.

item.title: Setting up your white-label copy
item.description: The steps from paying for a HabitForge licence to your copy going live on your own domain with your name, logo and colours.

item.title: Updates and renewals for a HabitForge licence
item.description: What counts as an update, the six months included with every licence and buyout, and how renewing by licence key works.

item.title: Verify a HabitForge licence
item.description: Every licensed HabitForge copy serves a licence file. Check a licence by its key or by the domain the copy runs on.

item.title: Moving to HabitForge
item.description: Step-by-step guides for moving to HabitForge from other habit trackers, each with a dated table of prices and features and the sources behind it.

item.title: Moving from Do Habits to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from Do Habits to HabitForge: keep the CSV, turn several-times-a-day goals into one daily check-in, and use pause where you used vacation mode.

item.title: Moving from everyday to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from everyday to HabitForge: no new-tab board or email reminders here. Write down the habits on your board, re-add them, and expect a missed day to fray, not break.

item.title: Moving from Fabulous to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from Fabulous to HabitForge: no coach here. Turn the parts of your routine you still do unprompted into habits, and let AI draft the wording only when you ask.

item.title: Moving from Habitica to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from Habitica to HabitForge: your party, gear and quests stay behind. Which habits to bring, how to sort them into build, break and maintain, and the dated facts.

item.title: Moving from Habitify to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from Habitify to HabitForge: watch, Mac and stacked reminders stay behind. Turn each stacked reminder into a written cue and Off mode into pause.

item.title: Moving from HabitKit to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from HabitKit to HabitForge: you go from no account and nobody watching to a Google sign-in and a public profile you can switch off. Do that first.

item.title: Moving from HabitNow to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from HabitNow to HabitForge: only your habits come; tasks, calendar and timers need another home. Make the backup, leave the one-off tasks, re-add the rest by hand.

item.title: Moving from Loop Habit Tracker to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from Loop Habit Tracker to HabitForge: you trade a no-account app for a Google sign-in. Keep the CSV, re-add your habits, and see where the rope and Loop’s score agree.

item.title: Moving from Productive to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from Productive to HabitForge: templates and place-based reminders stay behind. Write your own habits, or let AI draft one you then save, and keep your paused habits paused.

item.title: Moving from Streaks to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from Streaks to HabitForge: on an iPhone you lose the widgets and Apple Health and use the web app. Who should not move, and how to bring 24 tasks across.

item.title: Moving from Strides to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from Strides to HabitForge: dated targets stay behind. Bring the daily and weekly habits, mark bad ones as break, and use a challenge where you had an accountability partner.

item.title: Moving from Way of Life to HabitForge
item.description: Moving from Way of Life to HabitForge: export the CSV or JSON on Android, turn red habits into break habits, and move each diary note into the habit’s cue.

item.title: HabitForge documentation
item.description: Official documentation for HabitForge, a habit tracker that draws your consistency as a rope: it thickens with what you keep and frays where you stopped.

item.title: The Android app
item.description: HabitForge on Android is a native app with over-the-air updates, so fixes reach you without a store release. Install it from Google Play.

item.title: Install and offline
item.description: HabitForge is a PWA — install it to your home screen from any browser and keep checking in offline. Check-ins made without a connection sync when you reconnect.

item.title: AI and Speak
item.description: HabitForge drafts a habit's loop, reads your week back, helps word a post, and turns what you say into suggested check-ins, habits and posts. Nothing is saved until you press Save.

item.title: Themes and customiser
item.description: HabitForge ships light and dark themes plus a customiser for appearance, accent colour, radius, scaling and font size. Your choices follow your account.

item.title: Get started
item.description: Open HabitForge in any browser, sign in with Google, and create your first habit. Sign-in is Google only, and the Android app is on Google Play.

item.title: Changelog
item.description: What is new in HabitForge, latest first: the 1.0 rebuild with offline check-ins, scored challenges, a generous free tier, and the pre-release history before it.

item.title: Support
item.description: How to get help with HabitForge: the in-app contact form, email the author, or open a docs issue. There is a free tier plus Pro and Family plans.

item.title: Page tours and How HabitForge works
item.description: Every main HabitForge page has a short tour behind the signpost button in the header, and the How HabitForge works page explains the whole app in six steps.

item.title: Achievements
item.description: Achievements are milestones HabitForge unlocks as you build habits — streaks, points, and consistency goals — each with a celebration moment and bonus points.

item.title: Analytics
item.description: HabitForge's analytics turn your check-in history into weekly charts, so you can see which habits are holding and where consistency is slipping.

item.title: Community
item.description: HabitForge's community adds a board, challenges, friends and a leaderboard, with report and block tools. A new profile is visible by default; you can change it.

item.title: Reminders and notifications
item.description: An in-app bell tells you what happened while you were away, and your own device raises the reminders: one a day, and one per habit on the days it is due.

item.title: Check-ins and streaks
item.description: A check-in tells HabitForge you did a habit today. Consecutive check-ins build a streak and earn points, and your longest streak is kept even when a run breaks.

item.title: Create a habit
item.description: Create a habit with a name, category, kind and schedule, plus the optional cue, routine, reward, craving and investment fields from The Power of Habit.

item.title: Levels and points
item.description: Points come from check-ins and achievements across all your habits, and enough of them raise your level through ten forge tiers, from Spark to Forge Master.

item.title: Manage habits
item.description: Edit a habit's details, pause it while you are away, or delete it for good. Pausing keeps your history; deleting removes the habit permanently.

item.title: Rope strength
item.description: HabitForge's habit-strength meter. The rope thickens from a thread towards a chain as you keep going, and frays where you stopped. Calculated, not predicted.

item.title: Privacy and terms
item.description: Where to read HabitForge's privacy policy and terms, how sign-in and data work, and how to export or delete your account. Sign-in is Google-only.
